system:
You are the analysis agent of a reporting platform for Australia's threatened species. Conservation practitioners — people in government agencies, NGOs and recovery teams who decide where to survey, what to protect and what to escalate — read what you produce. You have read-only SQL access to the platform's database and produce insights from it, each grounded in queries you ran.

# The data

PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3.5. The corpus is every occurrence record the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) tags as nationally threatened (EPBC Critically Endangered, Endangered or Vulnerable), observed January 2015 to 2026-09-30, from one bulk download (DOI 10.26197/ala.40eee344-07ce-48d2-9ec2-be39574ff4c7): about 2.1 million records, 1,850 taxa, 300+ contributing datasets. Alongside it are all-taxa effort counts per 0.1° cell per month for the same period.

corpus.analysable_occurrences — VIEW — the records to analyse: occurrences that are valid, dated, and not from telemetry (animal-tracking) datasets. Includes dataset_kind ('wild' or 'managed'). Prefer this over occurrences.
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, occurrence_remarks text, event_remarks text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, dataset_kind text

corpus.datasets — TABLE — contributing datasets; kind is 'wild', 'managed' (fenced havens, reintroductions) or 'telemetry' (excluded from analysable_occurrences).
  columns: data_resource_uid text, name text, kind text, kind_reason text, first_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.effort_cells — TABLE — ALL-taxa record counts (threatened or not, telemetry excluded) per 0.1° cell per month: the denominator for reporting rates. Join on cell_lat/cell_lon and month.
  columns: cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, period_start date, period_end date, records integer, harvest_id text

corpus.harvest_runs — TABLE — provenance of each harvest (the corpus download and the effort counts).
  columns: harvest_id text, harvest_key text, run_id text, source text, description text, query jsonb, started_at timestamp with time zone, finished_at timestamp with time zone, expected_records integer, retrieved_records integer, complete boolean, corpus_hash text, request_count integer, warnings jsonb, analysis jsonb, loaded_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.occurrences — TABLE — every canonical occurrence record, telemetry included. geom is a PostGIS Point (SRID 4326); cell_lat/cell_lon are the 0.1° grid cell (rounded to nearest, as ALA assigns them).
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, occurrence_remarks text, event_remarks text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric

corpus.taxa — TABLE — one row per taxon (key taxon_concept_id); national_status is the EPBC status ALA attached.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, taxon_rank text, kingdom text, phylum text, taxon_class text, taxon_order text, family text, genus text, national_status text, status_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.taxon_tiers — VIEW — per taxon: analysable records since 2015, last record date, and statistical_tier (≥100 records since 2015).
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, records_since_2015 bigint, last_record_at timestamp with time zone, statistical_tier boolean

Useful facts: EPSG:3577 (Australian Albers, equal-area, metres) is available for gridding and areas; ibra_region is the IBRA 7 bioregion (null offshore — IBRA covers land only); coordinate_uncertainty_m is the radius the true position may lie within.

# Known properties of this data — read before interpreting anything

- **Records measure effort as much as animals.** These are mostly opportunistic records. All-taxa recording roughly doubled between 2017–19 and 2022–24 (about 1.9×), so counts and range measures grow with effort. Use corpus.effort_cells as a denominator where it matters.
- **Recent months are incomplete.** Datasets reach ALA months to a year late: January–August 2026 holds about 20% of the records January–August 2024 holds, and eBird (the largest dataset) has not loaded 2026 at all. A recent decline is not evidence of anything until this is accounted for.
- **Sources start and stop.** A compilation that ends in 2020, or a targeted survey wound up inside an ongoing state atlas, looks exactly like range loss. Check which datasets carry a taxon's records in each period before calling a change real.
- **Locations vary in precision.** About half the analysable records are located to within 2 km; about a third state no uncertainty; ALA generalises many sensitive species to roughly 10 km.
- **Managed populations** (dataset_kind = 'managed', e.g. fenced havens and reintroductions) are in the analysable view and are not wild trend.
- **National status** is as ALA attached it. Never infer, change or second-guess a taxon's conservation status.
- Taxonomy can shift: a taxon "disappearing" from a region can be a name re-assignment.

# How to work

- Call run_sql with one SELECT (or WITH … SELECT) per call, no trailing statements. Results are capped at 200 rows and queries time out after 30 s, so aggregate in SQL rather than pulling rows. Each call returns a query_id.
- Record each insight with record_insight as soon as it is established. Every insight cites the query_ids whose results support it, and every number in it must be a value those queries returned or simple arithmetic on them. Do not state figures you did not query.
- taxon_concept_id must be copied exactly from corpus.taxa; region is an IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for a national insight; period_start and period_end are the window the insight describes.
- Say how confident you are and why, in the confidence field: record counts, the datasets involved, effort, precision, and any artefact that could explain the pattern.
- When you have recorded everything worth recording, stop.

tools.name: run_sql
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL query (a single SELECT or WITH … SELECT) against the corpus. Returns a query_id, the columns and up to 200 rows. Cite the query_id in any insight that relies on the result.

sql.description: One SELECT or WITH … SELECT statement.

purpose.description: One line: what this query is for.

tools.name: record_insight
tools.description: Record one insight. Every figure must come from the cited queries.

category.description: A short label of your own for the kind of insight.

taxon_concept_id.description: Exactly as in corpus.taxa, or null for a non-taxon insight.

region.description: IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for national.

period_start.description: YYYY-MM-DD — start of the window the insight describes.

figures.description: The numbers behind the insight, as returned by your queries.

confidence.description: Why this should or should not be trusted: records, datasets, effort, precision, possible artefacts.

summary.description: One or two sentences a practitioner can act on.

query_ids.description: The run_sql query_ids whose results support this insight.

messages.content:
It is October 2026. A conservation practitioner responsible for Australia's threatened species asks: from this data, what should I know right now — what has changed, what is concerning, what is new, and where are we blind?

Investigate as you judge best and record each insight worth their attention — aim for the most important 20 to 40. For each, be explicit about confidence and about any data artefact that could explain the pattern.

WITH occ AS (
 SELECT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_date>='2017-01-01' AND event_date<'2020-01-01') na,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_date>='2022-01-01' AND event_date<'2025-01-01') nb
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE dataset_kind='wild' AND event_date>='2017-01-01' AND event_date<'2025-01-01'
   AND NOT (event_date>='2020-01-01' AND event_date<'2022-01-01')
 GROUP BY 1,2,3),
eff AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon, sum(records) FILTER (WHERE period_start<'2020-01-01' AND period_start>='2017-01-01') ea,
  sum(records) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01') eb FROM corpus.effort_cells GROUP BY 1,2),
agg AS (SELECT o.taxon_concept_id, sum(na) na, sum(nb) nb, sum(ea) ea, sum(eb) eb, count(*) FILTER (WHERE na>0) ca, count(*) FILTER (WHERE nb>0) cb
 FROM occ o LEFT JOIN eff e USING (cell_lat,cell_lon) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, na, nb, ca, cb,
 round((nb::numeric/nullif(eb,0))/nullif(na::numeric/nullif(ea,0),0),2) rr_ratio
FROM agg JOIN corpus.taxa t USING(taxon_concept_id)
WHERE na>=150 AND nb>=0
ORDER BY rr_ratio ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 40

input.summary: Since 2020 the record has gone almost dark for threatened mammals in the Northern Territory. Fauna Atlas N.T. delivered 3,070 threatened records in 2019 and 1 in 2024, so Djintamoonga, Arnhem Land Rock-rat and Northern Brushtail Possum look as if they have collapsed. That is an artefact of the atlas stopping, but it also means there is no current evidence on these taxa from ALA. Ask NT DEPWS for recent survey data directly before making any decision.

input.summary: This corpus barely covers threatened plants outside NSW. WITH occ AS (
 SELECT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_date>='2017-01-01' AND event_date<'2020-01-01') na,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_date>='2022-01-01' AND event_date<'2025-01-01') nb
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE dataset_kind='wild' AND data_resource_uid IN ('dr2009','dr368','dr359','dr1411','dr1097','dr365')
   AND event_date>='2017-01-01' AND event_date<'2025-01-01'
 GROUP BY 1,2,3),
eff AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon, sum(records) FILTER (WHERE period_start<'2020-01-01' AND period_start>='2017-01-01') ea,
  sum(records) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01') eb FROM corpus.effort_cells WHERE period_start>='2017-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1,2),
agg AS (SELECT o.taxon_concept_id, sum(na) na, sum(nb) nb, sum(ea) ea, sum(eb) eb, count(*) FILTER (WHERE na>0) ca, count(*) FILTER (WHERE nb>0) cb
 FROM occ o LEFT JOIN eff e USING (cell_lat,cell_lon) GROUP BY 1)
SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, t.taxon_class, na, nb, ca, cb,
 round((nb::numeric/nullif(eb,0))/nullif(na::numeric/nullif(ea,0),0),2) rr_ratio
FROM agg JOIN corpus.taxa t USING(taxon_concept_id)
WHERE nb>=300 AND cb>=15

input.summary: About 217,000 NSW BioNet records of reintroduced mammals in fenced havens are labelled 'wild' — about 10% of the whole corpus. They cover Bilby, Bridled Nailtail Wallaby, Shark Bay Burrowing Bettong, Woylie, Numbat and others, recorded at Pilliga (Brigalow Belt South), Mallee Cliffs (Murray Darling Depression) and Sturt (Simpson Strzelecki Dunefields). The apparent 7-fold 'wild' Bilby increase is entirely fenced-haven monitoring. Exclude these cells from any wild-trend or range analysis, and reclassify these records as managed.

confidence.level: high that these are effort artefacts

Opportunistic eBird records of bittern in NSW were flat (214 to 191) while effort nearly doubled.

input.summary: The biggest apparent increases among threatened animals are survey programmes, not recoveries. Australasian Bittern records rose about 8.6-fold, driven by Birdata in SA (63 to 6,528) and Victoria (121 to 3,026). Kangaroo Island Dunnart and Pygmy Blue-tongue rose 24-fold and 23-fold, both in SA Fauna. Don't report these as recoveries. The one opportunistic signal available, NSW eBird bittern records, was flat while effort roughly doubled.

input.summary: Much of the arid and northern interior is close to unobserved for threatened species: fewer than 200 records over nearly 12 years in Little Sandy Desert, Gibson Desert, Central Arnhem, Gascoyne, Great Victoria Desert, Central Ranges, Hampton and Tanami. Tanami fell from 153 records (2017–19) to 6 (2022–24), and Arnhem Plateau from 437 to 66. Several arid regions get about 90% of their records from eBird. Partnerships with Indigenous ranger groups and pastoral-zone surveys are the obvious way to fill this gap.

confidence.why: Counts come from the taxon_tiers view. Fewer than 10 records over nearly 12 years means no trend can be estimated from this data. Some of these taxa have sensitive locations withheld, or are monitored by agencies that do not share data with ALA.

input.summary: Of 392 Critically Endangered taxa, 178 have fewer than 10 records since 2015 (53 of 112 animals, 125 of 280 plants). Only 86 have the 100 or more records needed for statistical treatment, and 45 have no record since before 2020. For most Critically Endangered taxa this data cannot show change, so absence of an alert here is not reassurance. Prioritise targeted surveys or data-sharing agreements for these taxa.

WITH occ AS (
 SELECT taxon_concept_id, data_resource_uid ds, cell_lat, cell_lon,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_date>='2017-01-01' AND event_date<'2020-01-01') na,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE event_date>='2022-01-01' AND event_date<'2025-01-01') nb
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a JOIN corpus.taxa t USING(taxon_concept_id) WHERE t.taxon_class='Aves' AND dataset_kind='wild' AND data_resource_uid IN ('dr2009','dr359','dr368')
   AND event_date>='2017-01-01' AND event_date<'2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4),
eff AS (SELECT cell_lat, cell_lon, sum(records) FILTER (WHERE period_start<'2020-01-01' AND period_start>='2017-01-01') ea,
  sum(records) FILTER (WHERE period_start>='2022-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01') eb FROM corpus.effort_cells WHERE period_start>='2017-01-01' AND period_start<'2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1,2),
agg AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ds, sum(na) na, sum(nb) nb, (sum(nb)::numeric/sum(eb))/nullif(sum(na)::numeric/sum(ea),0) rr FROM occ LEFT JOIN eff USING(cell_lat,cell_lon) GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status,
 max(na) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr2009') eb_a, max(nb) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr2009') eb_b, round(max(rr) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr2009'),2) eb_rr,
 max(na) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr359') bd_a, max(nb) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr359') bd_b, round(max(rr) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr359'),2) bd_rr,
 max(na) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr368') bn_a, max(nb) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr368') bn_b, round(max(rr) FILTER (WHERE ds='dr368'),2) bn_rr

I recorded 31 insights, each tied to the queries behind it. Two need fixing:
- **Regent Honeyeater duplicate:** the first entry has no taxon ID; the second one, with the ID, should be kept.
- **New-taxa duplicate:** the first entry has a wrong figure (627 where 61 belonged); the version marked "(corrected)" replaces it.

The main thing to know is that this data now shows recording effort and data supply more clearly than species change. Many of the biggest apparent changes are artefacts, and only a few look like real declines.

**What's actually concerning (moderate confidence)**
- **Regent Honeyeater (Critically Endangered):** occupied 0.1° cells halved, from 122 in 2017–19 to 63 in 2022–24, while recording effort in those cells rose 1.81 times. The drop shows independently in BioNet and Birdata.
- **Painted Honeyeater:** effort-adjusted reporting fell in all three ongoing sources (eBird 0.70, Birdata 0.28, BioNet 0.22 of earlier levels). It is nomadic, so confirm over a longer window before escalating.
- **Wetland migratory birds:** Curlew Sandpiper and Latham's Snipe records stayed flat while effort nearly doubled, and summed bird counts fell. Similar species such as Eastern Curlew and Great Knot rose.
- **Swift Parrot:** the sources disagree (eBird stable, Birdata and BioNet down), so this data can't tell you whether it is declining.
- **No decline signal:** Gang-gang Cockatoo and Southern Greater Glider show no effort-adjusted decline, though records can't detect drops in density.

**What has changed or is new**
- **Reporting lag:** treat 2024 as the last complete year. eBird has nothing after 30 August 2025; iNaturalist is the only major source that is current.
- **iNaturalist:** 101 threatened taxa appeared in the data for the first time since 2023, 61 of them only through iNaturalist.
- **Plains-wanderer:** records in Queensland's Mitchell Grass Downs since 2024, a bioregion with none in 2015–2023. These are imprecise and need verifying.
- **Reintroductions:** these appear as new range, e.g. Woylie and Numbat on the Yorke Peninsula, and Shark Bay Burrowing Bettong at Sturt.
- **Myrtle-rust-threatened plants:** survey attention has surged, which reflects effort, not recovery.

**Artefacts that look like change**
- **Fenced havens labelled wild:** about 217,000 NSW BioNet records from fenced havens and reintroductions are labelled 'wild', about 10% of the corpus. This includes the apparent 7-fold Bilby increase.
- **Victorian atlas:** its bird and insect contributions collapsed, which distorts Victorian bird trends and the Golden Sun Moth.
- **Sources that stopped:** Northern Territory mammals, Lesser Sand Plover, Spotted Handfish and Grey-headed Flying-fox all look like collapses because a dataset stopped or a one-off survey surge ended.
- **Survey programmes:** the biggest "increases" (Australasian Bittern, Kangaroo Island Dunnart, Pygmy Blue-tongue) are dedicated surveys starting, not recoveries.

**Where you are blind**
- **Koala and Southern Cassowary:** effectively absent (8 and 3 records), because they are listed as populations and ALA doesn't tag the species-level records as threatened.
- **Northern Territory:** threatened fauna has been almost unrecorded since its state atlas stopped. River sharks and sawfish have no current records.
- **Other states:** plants are barely covered in WA, Tasmania and Queensland, and arid and northern bioregions are near-unobserved.
- **eBird gaps:** eBird contributes nothing for subspecies-listed and sensitive birds.
- **Haven-only species:** Central Rock-rat, Mernine and Woylie records come almost entirely from fenced havens, so there is no information on wild populations.
- **Critically Endangered taxa:** 178 of 392 have fewer than 10 records, and 51.8% of their records state no location precision.
- **Effort concentration:** the busiest 1% of cells hold 54.8% of all recording.
